services.name: Voice-Activated CRM · Sandbox Pilot
services.desc: Morning outbound call updates Nick’s NG project records by voice — read back, confirmed, audited.
services.detail: The first concrete voice pilot, requested by Nick Garrish (Account Director). Between 08:30 and 09:30 the system calls Nick, reads out his highest-priority or most out-of-date projects, takes the updates by voice, reads each proposed change back for explicit confirmation, and only then writes it to a SharePoint sandbox List. Every change is journalled (old value, new value, time, user, source) and a daily summary is emailed. A custom Azure application is the workflow owner — Microsoft Graph is the data path into Microsoft 365, not the application, and the speech/AI layer never writes records directly. Scope is deliberately narrow: the sandbox List only, records whose AM Owner is exactly NG, and the live project tracker in Teams is untouched until testing is approved.

sections.title: Microsoft Graph
sections.body: Reads and updates the selected SharePoint sandbox List. Access is granted to the application explicitly (selected-permissions consent) — no live-tracker permission is requested. No additional licence beyond the existing Microsoft 365 access.

sections.title: Azure Communication Services
sections.body: Places and controls the outbound telephone call — dialling Nick’s mobile, playing prompts, receiving voice input, raising call events. ACS provides the telephone connection only; the conversation and all business logic sit in the application.

sections.title: Speech and AI
sections.body: Azure AI Speech for listening and speaking, and an Azure-hosted language model for interpretation. This layer interprets and responds — it makes no record writes of its own.

sections.title: Custom Azure application
sections.body: Python or C#, hosted in Azure. Schedules the call and selects the authorised NG projects, co-ordinates telephony + speech + AI, validates proposed changes, reads them back and obtains explicit confirmation, writes through Graph handling concurrent edits and retries safely, records the audit trail, co-ordinates report refreshes and sends the daily summary.

sections.title: SharePoint List
sections.body: Structured sandbox records with required unique Project IDs, owner identity, status and next actions — defined fields, per-record forms, status views and version history. Use status views rather than moving or deleting records. Excel is retained as a reporting output, not the system of record.

sections.title: Scheduling
sections.body: An Azure timer or Power Automate — use one scheduler, not both. Premium licensing is not required for the pilot: the Azure application schedules the calls and performs the updates directly. Assess Premium only if a selected flow genuinely requires it.

sections.title: Audit and monitoring
sections.body: Pending and completed updates are recorded durably so a retry can never repeat a saved change. Failed writes, audit steps or report refreshes report their actual outcome — never a false “complete”. Raw call recording is not required by default.

sections.title: Approval and boundaries
sections.body: IT and the SharePoint owner approve the sandbox, restrict human and application access, and enable version history. The application re-checks the NG owner and the record version at every update — a filtered view alone is not security. Nick is authenticated before any confidential project detail is read out.

sections.title: Sage X3 — later, separate approval
sections.body: A separate service using Sage-supported interfaces, read-only initially (customer code, order status, invoiced value). Field ownership and stable ID mappings to be agreed with the X3 team ahead of the 4 January go-live. Tracker completion or hold status must never automatically close or alter an ERP order; live writeback requires a separately approved scope.

sections.title: Not required for the pilot
sections.body: Copilot Studio voice capabilities and Office Scripts. Office Scripts are not needed for List updates and should not be assumed to refresh every workbook connection or pivot table — consider them only for specific Excel reporting tasks.

sections.title: Indicative running cost
sections.body: One user, a 10–15 minute call on roughly 22 working days a month: an initial £50–£150 per month Azure operating allowance covers consumption-based voice, AI and application hosting. IT to confirm the selected services and tariffs before approval.

inputs: SharePoint sandbox List records (AM Owner = NG)
Sage X3 customer / order data (later, read-only)
outputs: Confirmed record updates in the sandbox List
Update journal (old / new value, confirmation, outcome)
Refreshed sandbox reporting (Excel or Power BI)
Daily email — saved changes, failed changes, outstanding actions
services.phase: Proposed · sandbox pilot — gated on IT approval and SharePoint access

services.name: BrightHR Ingestion → InVentry
services.desc: On-demand pull of staff roster from BrightHR into InVentry tablets.
services.detail:
COO-driven on-demand sync. Pulls the active staff roster from BrightHR (Personal Access Token or client_credentials OAuth), writes the InVentry-format CSV (First Name, Surname, Email Address) to the watched folder where InVentry’s service picks it up. Every pull is snapshotted to disk for audit. Guards: refuses to write if zero records are returned or if the dropout exceeds the configured threshold (default 30%). Live attendance (Blip clock-ins) is a separate, later feature once BrightHR API access exposes it.
COO controls
Buttons activate as soon as BrightHR credentials and the employee endpoint are populated in .env. They call POST /api/hr/sync, /api/hr/pull and /api/hr/load respectively.
outputs: InVentry CSV at the watched folder
services.phase: Built — gated on BrightHR API credentials
services.invoke: Once API access is granted: the COO or any director with permission clicks Run Sync above. Also schedulable from Windows Task Scheduler. Endpoints: POST /api/hr/sync (pull+load), /api/hr/pull, /api/hr/load.

services.name: WeAreSDI · Public-Site AI Layer
services.desc: Layered AI-readiness on the existing WordPress site — not a rewrite.
services.detail: WordPress is the right engine for what SDI is doing — AI search engines love it for clean HTML, schema/JSON-LD support and B2B-intel integrations. Rather than rewrite the site, we layer six AI-native upgrades on top, and use this portal to mock new sections privately before they touch the staging WordPress clone.

sections.title: 1 · LinkedIn → site insights feed
sections.body: Publish once on LinkedIn, syndicate automatically to a News / Insights section on wearesdi.com so AI crawlers see fresh SDI activity immediately. Tools: Elfsight feed widget or Jetpack Social with a filter on the relevant topics.

sections.title: 2 · AI-native SEO & content
sections.body: Adopt an AI SEO plugin — Rank Math with Content AI, or AIOSEO. These optimise for the technical vocabulary engineers and procurement people actually search, so SDI ranks for the high-intent, long-tail prompts AI search engines surface.

sections.title: 3 · RAG chatbot on site
sections.body: A retrieval-augmented chatbot (e.g. MxChat) trained on SDI’s own technical docs and case studies. Acts as a 24/7 technical sales assistant or "AI product expert" — not a generic FAQ bot. Same RAG pattern already running in the estimating engine.

sections.title: 4 · GA4 + B2B visitor identification
sections.body: GA4 wired to Sage X3 (when ready). Layer a B2B visitor-ID tool on top to surface which companies read which pages. Dealfront (Leadfeeder + Echobot, EU-built, GDPR-aligned) is the recommended path for the UK — Clearbit folded into HubSpot’s Breeze Intelligence and is no longer a standalone option. Albacross is an alternative. Track stakeholder journeys (multiple visitors from one prospect company) and conversion attribution back to the originating content.

sections.title: 5 · Predictive next-best content
sections.body: AI suggests the most relevant follow-up content to each visitor based on the current page — e.g. a Vue case study automatically surfaced when someone reads the cinema-display capability page. Lifts engagement and quote-request conversion.

sections.title: 6 · Multimodal search optimisation
sections.body: Tag SDI’s video and high-res facility imagery with ImageObject / VideoObject schema so AI tools can "see" the facility and processes, not just read text. Alt text, captions, transcripts — all built for AI ingestion as well as accessibility.

services.name: OBS Studio · Live Recording
services.desc: Professional screen recording and live streaming — AI demos, presentations, facility content and virtual camera for Teams.
services.detail: OBS (Open Broadcaster Software) is the capture and broadcast layer at SDI. Record AI tool demos, estimating engine runs, design presentations and facility walkthroughs for the portal, SEEN content and client materials. Free, open source, runs locally. Download from obsproject.com if not already installed.

sections.title: First-time setup
sections.body: Settings → Video: Base Resolution 1920×1080, Output 1920×1080, FPS 30. Settings → Output → Recording: Format MP4, set a recordings folder (e.g. C:\SDIRecordings). Settings → Audio: Desktop Audio = your speakers; Mic = your microphone. Encoder: NVENC if you have an NVIDIA GPU (faster, no CPU hit), otherwise x264.

sections.title: Scene · AI Demo / Estimating Engine
sections.body: Add Scene “Engine Demo”. Sources → + → Display Capture (full screen). Add Audio Input Capture (your microphone). Press Start Recording before running the engine. Stop when done. The MP4 lands in your configured recordings folder. Use this for parity run walkthroughs and portal demonstrations.

sections.title: Scene · Presentation (screen + face cam)
sections.body: Add Scene “Presentation”. Sources: Window Capture (select your slides or browser) + Video Capture Device (webcam) + Audio Input. Drag the webcam source to the bottom-right and resize it. Use for recording portal walkthroughs, AI tool demonstrations or client-facing demos.

sections.title: Scene · Facility Walkthrough
sections.body: Add Scene “Facility”. Sources: Video Capture Device (GoPro via USB, external camera or built-in laptop camera). Set output resolution to match your camera. Exports as MP4 for LinkedIn video, the SEEN newsletter or the wearesdi.com media library.

sections.title: Virtual Camera → Teams / Zoom / Meet
sections.body: Tools → VirtualCam → Start Virtual Camera. In Teams: Settings → Devices → Camera → select OBS Virtual Camera. Everything in your active OBS scene broadcasts live into the call — switch scenes mid-call to share different layouts. If Virtual Camera isn’t shown, install the obs-virtualcam plugin (free, GitHub).

sections.title: Streaming live · LinkedIn Live / YouTube
sections.body: Settings → Stream: select YouTube or Custom RTMP for LinkedIn Live. Paste your stream key from YouTube Studio or LinkedIn Live Events (you need to create the live event in advance on each platform to get the key). Press Start Streaming. OBS handles encoding; the platform handles distribution.

sections.title: Hotkeys worth setting
sections.body: Settings → Hotkeys. Recommended: Ctrl+Shift+R Start/Stop Recording, Ctrl+Shift+S Start/Stop Streaming, F1, F2… per scene. Hotkeys fire even when OBS is minimised — useful when the engine is running full-screen and you need to stop recording without switching windows.

inputs: Webcam or external camera (GoPro, USB cam)
Stream key for LinkedIn Live or YouTube
outputs: Virtual camera feed into Teams / Zoom / Meet
services.invoke: Launch OBS from the desktop. Select the right scene for the task, hit Start Recording or Start Streaming. Recordings land in your configured output folder (Settings → Output → Recording Path). Stop recording before closing the engine window.

services.name: AI Tech Radar
services.desc: Continuous intelligence scan of the global AI marketplace, tuned to SDI’s stack.
services.detail: A standing, evidence-based view of where AI is heading across SDI’s entire technology stack. Uses Claude Opus 4.8 with live web search to track the newest large language models, OCR and document-extraction engines, computer-vision systems, geometry and mathematical estimating models, 3D and generative-design tools, and simulation platforms including NVIDIA Omniverse and digital twins. Each finding is assessed against how SDI actually works — the estimating engine, the co-worker agents and the design studio — and tagged ADOPT, TRIAL, ASSESS or HOLD so leadership can see at a glance what is proven, what is worth piloting and what to keep watching. Every run flags only what has changed since the last, giving the MD a true "what’s new" view. Runs on demand and can be scheduled weekly via Windows Task Scheduler.
outputs: Dated HTML radar report → Status Reports
ADOPT / TRIAL / ASSESS / HOLD rings per area
services.phase: Live — ten areas, six in the default run
services.invoke: Run python tech_radar.py on the engine host (--full for all areas). Reports land in output\reports and surface in Status Reports.
